body: A digital computer represents instructions and values as discrete states. In a stored-program design, a processor reads instructions from memory and follows them to change or compare stored values. An input acquires data from outside the machine. An output sends a result to a person or another device.

An artificial intelligence system can produce predictions, classifications, recommendations or other outputs for a specified purpose. In one common approach, machine learning uses examples to fit a model that can produce outputs on new data. Performance can change when data and conditions differ from those used to develop the system.
credit: Centauri Archive editorial draft, written with AI assistance
limitations: An output needs evaluation against evidence and its intended use. Behaving as if it understands a symbol gives limited evidence about what processes the system uses.
purpose: Connect representational data and instructions to computation and model limits.

revision_history.change: Explained stored programs and prediction limits without unsupported claims about machine consciousness
